source: Company shareholding-pattern filings to NSE under SEBI's listing regulations (table III), valued at NSE month-end market capitalisation; EPFR++ source in_shp
note: Every company listed on the NSE tells the exchange each quarter who holds its shares, as a share of all its shares. This book values those shares at the company's NSE market value for the quarter's last month and adds up every company with a filing. Promoters are the families, parent companies and governments that control a company; everyone else is the public. Indian institutions are mainly mutual funds, insurers and pension funds; foreign institutions are mainly foreign portfolio investors. The "of which" lines are parts of the rows above and are never added again. A few filings list owners adding to far more than the company itself (BSE LIMITED); each such company is counted whole in its own row rather than spread across owners. Amounts are in rupees, and ₹1 trillion is ₹1 lakh crore. Rupee values start in March 2024, the first month with exact NSE market values; June 2026 is the newest quarter with nearly all filings in, and its companies make up 98.9% of the NSE's listed value. Technical detail: SEBI shareholding-pattern filings (table III of the XBRL filing) as the terminal stores them, the filed group lines, and NSE month-end market capitalisation; a filing whose promoter, public and non-promoter non-public lines miss 100% by more than a point is kept whole in its own row.
